glosses: o sowie, puchaczu wydawać głuche dźwięki

examples.text: Cyrkowa widownia pohukiwała głośno i radośnie.
Przestałbyś już na niego pohukiwać, on się nie zmieni.
My performance drew hoots of derision from the crowd.
I heard the hoot of an owl.
The party at the weekend was such a hoot! Thanks for the invite.

glosses: A small particle; a whit or jot.

examples.text: We don't care a hoot about what you think.
Well, it was Sunday morning, and the wheat nothing like ripe; but it was a chance, and I got onto my reaper and banged down every hoot of it before Monday night.

glosses: To cry out or shout in contempt.

examples.text: Matrons and girls shall hoot at thee no more,

glosses: To make a hoo, the cry of an owl.

examples.text: The clamorous owl that nightly hoots and wonders / At our quaint spirits.
Outside an owl was hooting most dismally in the darkness. The villa was on a by-road, and there was no human sound to link them up with life.

glosses: To assail with contemptuous cries or shouts; to follow with derisive shouts.

examples.text: Mary felt extremely offended when the workers hooted at her.
And I will be content, that Partridge, and the rest of his Clan, may hoot me for a Cheat and Impostor, if I fail in any single Particular of Moment.

glosses: To sound the horn of a vehicle.

examples.text: When you arrive to pick me up, hoot, and I'll come outside.

glosses: Money, especially in the form of cash given as payment.

examples.text: On the construction you could make a pot of hoot in no time. You oughter be able to get two or three quid a day when things is busy.
